column1: # The Sassembly application entry contract — ADR-0015 clause A1, task `F-001e1`,
# ADR-0015: "An application is entered at the ELF `e_entry` *by a loader*, with a
# stack pointer it did not choose and its arguments in a defined place. It does
# not run because the machine was reset to it, and it does not know its own load
# This file says what "a defined place" is. It is the whole integer register file
# at the instant the loader's `sret` lands on `e_entry` — all 32, because a
# contract that names three registers and says "the rest are whatever" is not a
# contract, and a program that reads `s3` and finds the loader's leftovers is a
# program that works until the loader changes.
#   sp   the loader mapped this stack and chose this address. A1's "a stack
#        pointer it did not choose" is the whole difference from a boot proof,
#        which sets `sp` from a linker symbol it can see.
#   ra   ZERO, and that is deliberate. There is nowhere to return to: an
#        application ends by CALLING call 0, not by returning from `e_entry`.
#        Returning jumps to 0, which is not mapped, which is a fetch page fault
#        the supervisor reports — a diagnosable bug rather than a silent exit.
#        This is A5 in one register.
#   a1   the handle vector. Every surface an application may touch (A4) arrives
#        here, by number, and there is no other way to obtain one. Nothing is
#        ambient (doc 07 §3). A program handed nothing can do nothing but exit.
# WHAT IS NOT HERE, AND WHY. There is no argv, no environment block and no
# auxiliary vector. A Sassembly application's inputs are capabilities, not
# strings: doc 07 §3 declares requirements in the source and the loader grants
# them, so `a0`/`a1` carry the grant. A string an application needs is read
# through a handle like any other input.
# The `at-entry` column is one of: `0` (the register holds zero), or a name
# the numbers are not typed here twice.

column4: no return address: an application exits by call 0, and returning from e_entry is a fetch fault at 0
top of the stack the loader mapped, 16-byte aligned; the program did not choose it
no global pointer; a program that wants one computes it
no thread pointer; a program that wants one computes it
how many handles the loader granted, 0 or more
address of a readable array of a0 u64 handles; the only way to obtain a surface
